messages:
tom_customer: Hey team — after the egress allowlist change this morning our prod app pods can no longer reach the internal service endpoint sns-prod.service.acme.internal. Apps see 502s and traces show DNS NXDOMAIN from the pod resolver. Started ~08:10 UTC. ticket: #12345

sara_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact repro steps? Are the failures only from prod pods or also from bastion? Any recent infra changes besides the allowlist?

tom_customer: Only change was the egress allowlist rolled at 08:05 (blocked several ranges). Repro steps: curl from pod to https://sns-prod.service.acme.internal -> fails. From host (bastion) curl works.

sara_support: Got it. Can you run these from a failing pod and paste output: 1) dig +short @10.10.50.7 sns-prod.service.acme.internal A 2) dig +short @169.254.169.253 sns-prod.service.acme.internal A 3) cat /etc/resolv.conf and kubectl get pods -o wide for the pod

-- pod output pasted by tom_customer --

tom_customer: Here you go:

/etc/resolv.conf:
search prod.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 10.96.0.10
options ndots:5

# dig to corporate recursive (used to work)
$ dig +short @10.10.50.7 sns-prod.service.acme.internal A
172.16.100.45

# dig to node-local / kube-dns resolver
$ dig +short @10.96.0.10 sns-prod.service.acme.internal A

# no answer -> caller sees NXDOMAIN

kubectl get pods -o wide | grep sns
sns-xxxx   1/1 Running   1    3m   10.2.5.12   ip-10-2-5-12

sara_support: Thanks — so corporate recursive returns A record but cluster resolver returns nothing. That points at forwarding path being blocked or a cache returning NXDOMAIN. @mike_sre can you check node-local-dns / CoreDNS config and whether UDP/53 egress to 10.10.50.7 is allowed from cluster nodes?

mike_sre: Looking now. Quick checks: 1) iptables/egress on nodes show rule to DROP to 10.10.50.0/24 for non-whitelisted apps (rolled out at 08:05). 2) node-local DNS (10.96.0.10) is configured to forward the service.acme.internal zone to 10.10.50.7 via stubDomains in CoreDNS. If forwarder is unreachable we get NXDOMAIN by design here because the cluster relies on the corporate override.

mike_sre: CoreDNS stubDomain snippet:

```
service.acme.internal:53 {
    forward . 10.10.50.7
}
```

mike_sre: There is also a note: we used conditional forwarder instead of Route53 Resolver endpoints because cross-account hosted zone is authoritative for that name.

jana_network: Confirmed egress allowlist blocked 10.10.50.7:53/udp from the node subnet. That was part of the tightened policy to block non-k8s egress ranges. Looks like the corporate resolver was accidentally removed from the allowlist.

sara_support: That would explain the behavior: bastion -> corporate resolver allowed so bastion sees A record, pods -> node resolver -> forward to corporate resolver blocked -> NXDOMAIN.

mike_sre: Quick repro from a node (telnet style check):
```
# from node
$ nc -u -zv 10.10.50.7 53
nc: connect to 10.10.50.7 port 53 (udp) failed: Operation timed out
```

mike_sre: If we re-open egress to 10.10.50.7:53 the forwarder answers and resolution should recover.

tom_customer: Can you patch in a hotfix? This is impacting production traffic.

jana_network: I'm going to request a temporary rule to allow 10.10.50.7/32 port 53 udp/tcp from the node subnets back in the allowlist. ETA 8 minutes.

dns-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0457 — "prod pods NXDOMAIN due to egress allowlist blocking corporate DNS forwarder". Assigned to jana_network, mike_sre.

sara_support: While that's being applied — workaround: set an explicit /etc/hosts entry in the service proxy container pointing sns-prod.service.acme.internal -> 172.16.100.45. Not ideal but can reduce downtime.

mike_sre: Jana — once rule is live I'll flush CoreDNS cache and verify from a pod:
```
kubectl exec -it sns-xxxx -- sh -c "kill -HUP $(pidof systemd-resolved) || true"
# or restart kube-dns pods
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
```

jana_network: Temporary allowlist applied at 08:24 UTC for 10.10.50.7/32:53 tcp/udp from node-subnets. Please verify.

mike_sre: Verified — after restart of coredns pods I see resolution restored:
```
$ kubectl exec -it sns-xxxx -- dig +short @10.96.0.10 sns-prod.service.acme.internal A
172.16.100.45
```

mike_sre: Application 502s cleared after ~30s of cache warmup.

tom_customer: Confirmed traffic is healthy again. Thanks for the fast turnaround :white_check_mark:

sara_support: Root cause: egress allowlist change removed corporate DNS forwarder; cluster relies on that forwarder for split-horizon records for service.acme.internal (corporate override / cross-account zone).

sara_support: Follow-ups:
- jana_network to add regression test to allowlist CI and add corporate resolver IPs to the whitelists with a tag.
- mike_sre to update runbook: detect NXDOMAIN spikes for internal service zones and auto-escalate to network.
- ops to evaluate moving to Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints or a resilient forwarding architecture.

jana_network: Noted. I'll leave the temporary allow for 24h and then propose a safer CIDR or managed tag approach.

mike_sre: Adding a quick diagnostic snippet to run if this happens again:
```
# from pod
dig +tcp @10.96.0.10 sns-prod.service.acme.internal A +time=2 +tries=1
# from node
nc -u -zv 10.10.50.7 53
# check coredns stub config
kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
```

sara_support: Closing ticket as resolved. Will keep INC-2026-0457 open for the follow-ups. :eyes:
